result.process_summary: Both the architectural blueprinting process and OOAD begin with a survey/analysis to identify entity types (classes) and their properties (attributes) and behaviors (methods). They then move to a design phase where a detailed plan (blueprint/model) is created, reusing standard components (inheritance), grouping related parts into cohesive units (encapsulation), and explicitly showing connections between entities (associations). The design also supports interchangeable configurations (polymorphism). Finally, visual representations are shared with stakeholders to ensure shared understanding and alignment before construction/implementation.
potential_breaks: Inheritance is portrayed as simple component reuse (bathroom layout), which may obscure the hierarchical type relationship central to inheritance.
Encapsulation is described as organizing sections of a blueprint, which may miss the crucial aspect of information hiding and access control.
Polymorphism likened to a modular kitchen simplifies the concept of dynamic method dispatch and substitutability.
